Please include the complete itinerary, both passengers currently on the booking, how many bags are already attached, whether insurance is included, and the payment history. Also, while you’re in that reservation, please check the current status of the outbound flight FLE7F420 for 2026-10-01 and tell me whether that segment still looks normal.
summary: A 14-turn airline + retail + device session for Maya (Lin) Chen. T1 reviews round-trip C4C633; T2–T3 rename a passenger (Maya Chen -> Maya Lin Chen); T4 reasons that a requested flight update is a no-op, and T5–T6 run it formally anyway (with heavy data-model patching) — which silently flips the insurance field from standard to no. At T7 the user catches this and the agent restores insurance and adds a checked bag (T8). T9 reviews the other booking EC4C1C, T10 texts Jordan Kim, and T11–T12 process a clothing return for Jordan Lee. T13 recaps C4C633 and T14 closes. Every recall probe (T3, T4, T12, T13, T14) is credited: the agent keeps C4C633 and EC4C1C distinct, remembers the renamed passenger, the restored insurance, and the correct return payment card without re-asking. The two sub-goal FAILs stem from grader expectations the agent correctly contradicted (a renamed passenger on the other booking; a category-specific return window the policy doesn't have).
